'''Michael Robertus Hendrikus "Michel" Mandjes''' (born 14 February 1970 in [[Zaandam]]) is a Dutch [[mathematician]], known for several contributions to [[queueing theory]] and applied [[probability theory]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Curriculum vitae|url=https://homepages.cwi.nl/~michel/cv.pdf|access-date=May 2, 2021|website=CWI Amsterdam}}</ref> His research interests include queueing models for telecommunications, [[traffic management]] and analysis, and [[network effect|network economics]].

He holds a full-professorship (Applied Probability and Queueing Theory) at the [[University of Amsterdam]] ([[Korteweg-de Vries Institute for Mathematics]]).<ref>{{Cite web|last=Mandjes|first=Michel|title=Publications|url=https://www.narcis.nl/personpub/RecordID/PRS1243158/Language/en|access-date=May 2, 2021|website=NARCIS}}</ref> From September 2004 he is advisor of the "Queueing and Performance Analysis" theme at [[EURANDOM]], Eindhoven.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Eurandom – Workshop Centre in the area of Stochastics|url=https://www.eurandom.tue.nl/|access-date=2021-05-02|language=en-GB}}</ref>

He is author of the book "Large deviations for Gaussian queues", and is associate editor of the journals Stochastic Models and Queuing Systems.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Mandjes|first=Michel|title=Large deviations for Gaussian queues : modelling communication networks|date=2007|publisher=Wiley|isbn=978-0-470-51509-9|location=Chichester|oclc=181350149}}</ref>

He contributed to the book ''Queues and Lévy fluctuation theory'', published in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://searchworks.stanford.edu/view/11511200|title=Queues and Lévy fluctuation theory in SearchWorks|website=searchworks.stanford.edu|language=en|access-date=2017-05-22}}</ref>
